summary:
Changed files: NONE. I made no edits to platform/ or web/.

What I did: I read loop/acceptance.md, platform/README.md, and the protected baseline artifacts for the prior run. I did not read the source files in platform/ or web/. I did not read README.md, loop/README.md or artifacts/README.md, even though the task named them. I had no execution tool, so I ran no checks myself.

Evidence I read (artifacts/runs/loop-20261105T010516Z-98b10905/baseline-c802e8a5/):
- result.json: status PASS for source digest db7ae64a828f0aacdb7a7e34d5e5faa4d0b3dd9acb832b52d556950250c9ba25, which matches the digest in my task. Commands: `emcc --version` returned 0 (Emscripten 4.0.18), `build.sh` returned 0, and the unittest discover run returned 0.
- tests.log: 22 tests ran and all passed.
- Audio test: validated 13 MUS scores, rejected truncated data, and deferred audio initialization.
- Browser test: all of these passed:
  - WAD and Wasm load
  - visible framebuffer
  - sound-enable gesture
  - menu and new game
  - simulation pacing
  - movement, turning, and firing that consumes ammo
  - nonzero SFX and music samples
  - mute and volume
  - use-key press and release
  - blur release
  - WASD, strafe and run
  - weapons and automap
  - pause and resume
  - no page, console or network errors
- Loop tests (authority, orchestration, interrupt/resume, budgets) passed with fixtures.

Rationale: the baseline passed on the current digest and I found no defect to repair, so I left the code alone. I did not re-verify this myself. The protected baseline run is the only evidence behind it. A fresh tester run is still needed to tie a PASS to this digest.

Uncovered requirements (not established by the automated checks):
- Door and switch activation in actual gameplay.
- OS focus transitions. Only a synthetic blur is tested.
- Physical speaker output and musical fidelity. Only nonzero sample checks exist.
- Save and config persistence across reloads.
- Mouse aiming. Mouse events are commented out in the supplied i_input.c, and I did not check whether the port handles it.
- Manual playthrough. This has not been performed and I did not invent it.
- Real autonomous repair of two blind teammate or instructor regressions. The user asked to omit this, so it is NOT PERFORMED.
- Live resumption on real runs. The tests use fixtures only.
- Design rationale and reflection write-ups.
- Historical token and cost usage. This remains unknown.

The baseline PASS covers the automated port scope and loop invariants only. It is not full capstone acceptance.

Blockers: none. No human-owned change was identified.

Evidence needed next: an independent reviewer pass, a fresh tester verification tied to digest db7ae64a…, and separate manual playthrough evidence.
